about: Shared test vectors of the review rules (README.md, "Review rules"). The Python tests (review_glob.test.py, review_judge.test.py) read this file, and the TypeScript side reads the same file: a change to the matching or the judge that updates one side only fails the other side's tests. Paths are made up. `globs`: [glob, path, matches]. `cases`: a config from `configs` (a whole `review` block, which must parse), the changed paths as `git diff --name-status -M` prints them ([status, path] or [R<score>|C<score>, old, new]), and the expected weight, required lenses (in order), rules hit (in rule order) and protected paths (in diff order). The config file is `config_path`. `findings`: a lens report body and what review_judge.read_findings reads in it ([kind, line] of each blocker or major, and whether it has a findings section); `group` says which rule it shows. `scans`: counted posts (by the lens author association, in order, `edited` and `hidden` as GitHub records them) and what lens.Review.lens_scan reads (the history of [name, sha] and each lens key's newest [sha, why]). `rounds`: review_judge.judge_rounds on a history, each lens key's newest entry [how, body], `decided`, and `changes` (sha -> what the pull request changes at it; a sha not listed is its own change). Every section is run by both sides: a test fails if one side meets a section or a vector it does not run.

a normal change
one critical file among normal ones needs the critical lenses only
a rename out of a critical folder counts under its old path
a rename into a critical folder counts under its new path
a delete counts
a copy counts under both paths
a mode-only or type change counts
the config file itself is critical
deleting the config file is critical
a lens prompt is critical though a light rule matches it
renaming a lens prompt is critical under its old path
a lens prompt that only the approach lens names is protected too
a workflow file is critical
a folder next to the workflows is not protected
an empty diff counts as the catch-all rule, never as no lens
a path written twice counts once
two critical rules hit: the lenses of both
** in the middle matches no segment and many
* does not cross /
two normal rules hit: the lenses of both, each once
* matches a dotfile
a catch-all written as */** takes a root file
a protected path takes the first critical rule even when another critical rule matches it
the config file among light changes
the empty diff with a critical catch-all
a protected path inside a light folder
light then normal by rule order
